raw:
{
  "items": [
    {
      "category": "support_location_extent",
      "entity": "Supported boundary Γu of the square plate",
      "issue": "figure_only",
      "description": "Sec. 4.1.1 refers to Fig. 6a without identifying the supported edges, positions, or lengths. The prescribed zero displacement itself is unambiguous.",
      "readings": [
        "Entire left edge",
        "Entire bottom edge",
        "Two left-edge patches covering y/L in [0,0.1] and [0.9,1]"
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "load_position",
      "entity": "Traction application boundary Γt",
      "issue": "figure_only",
      "description": "Sec. 4.1.1 describes asymmetric loading and refers to Fig. 6a, but gives neither application coordinates nor the number of loaded boundary segments.",
      "readings": [
        "One patch on the right edge centered at y/L=0.25",
        "One patch on the right edge centered at y/L=0.75",
        "One patch on the bottom edge centered at x/L=0.75",
        "Two patches on the right edge centered at y/L=0.25 and 0.5"
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "load_extent_distribution",
      "entity": "Length and discretization of each loaded boundary segment",
      "issue": "figure_only",
      "description": "Neither Sec. 4.1 nor Sec. 4.1.1 specifies the length of Γt. The stated traction magnitude therefore does not determine the resultant force or its distribution among grid nodes.",
      "readings": [
        "Uniform prescribed traction over a segment of length 0.02L",
        "Uniform prescribed traction over a segment of length 0.10L",
        "Uniform prescribed traction over one boundary grid edge, integrated into equivalent nodal forces"
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "load_direction",
      "entity": "Traction vector on Γt",
      "issue": "figure_only",
      "description": "Sec. 4.1 supplies the vector magnitude, but its direction for the asymmetrically loaded plate is left to Fig. 6a.",
      "readings": [
        "Vertically downward: t/|t|=(0,-1)",
        "Horizontally leftward: t/|t|=(-1,0)",
        "Diagonally downward and leftward: t/|t|=(-1,-1)/sqrt(2)"
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "passive_region",
      "entity": "Protection of material adjacent to loads and supports on the structured grid",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "The level-set formulation constrains a boundary set Gt, but Sec. 4.1.1 supplies no positive-area protection mask or rule for translating boundary protection into passive grid cells.",
      "readings": [
        "Constrain boundary level-set nodes only; no passive cells",
        "Keep one cell layer adjacent to the loaded boundary solid",
        "Keep one cell layer adjacent to both loaded and supported boundaries solid"
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "other",
      "entity": "Out-of-plane depth and conversion of the two-dimensional line traction",
      "issue": "vague",
      "description": "Sec. 2.1 specifies plane strain, while Sec. 4.1 gives bulk E in GPa and traction in N/m without explaining the depth or line-load conversion used for absolute compliance.",
      "readings": [
        "Unit depth of 1 m, with the stated traction treated as force per in-plane boundary length",
        "Constant depth of 0.01 m, with stiffness multiplied by depth and the same prescribed line traction"
      ],
      "effect": "scale_only"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "Individual β experiments in Sec. 4.1.1",
      "issue": "vague",
      "description": "Only the range β=2 to β=8 is stated; the discrete values used for the comparison are not listed.",
      "readings": [
        "Separate runs at β={2,8}",
        "Separate runs at β={2,4,6,8}",
        "Separate runs at β={2,3,4,5,6,7,8}"
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "material",
      "entity": "Characteristic function, Ersatz stiffness, and sensitivity in intermediate material",
      "issue": "conflicting",
      "description": "Eq. (23) makes Θ smooth, but Sec. 4.1 subsequently invokes binary identities to derive Eq. (41). For smooth Θ and q=3, the derivative of Eq. (40) contains Θ² rather than the Θ printed in Eq. (41).",
      "readings": [
        "Use smooth Θ for volume and cubic Ersatz stiffness, with derivative 3(1-e)Θ²",
        "Use smooth Θ for volume and cubic Ersatz stiffness, with the printed derivative 3(1-e)Θ",
        "Use binary Θ=1 for φ≥0 and zero otherwise in state and volume calculations, with Eq. (41)"
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "Numerical initial fields φ0 and φ−1",
      "issue": "vague",
      "description": "Sec. 4.1 specifies fully occupied initial geometries, but does not give the positive level-set values or explicitly specify their numerical equality for this experiment.",
      "readings": [
        "φ0=φ−1=1 throughout the interior",
        "φ0=φ−1=0.5 throughout the interior",
        "φ0=1 and φ−1=0.5 throughout the interior, giving nonzero initial evolution velocity"
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "Enforcement of the level-set range [-1,1]",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Sec. 2.1 defines the bounded range, but Sec. 3 gives a linear update without specifying how those bounds are enforced.",
      "readings": [
        "Clip nodal values to [-1,1] after every update",
        "Enforce box constraints while solving the update",
        "Rescale the updated field globally into [-1,1], then restore prescribed boundary values"
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "Level-set Dirichlet value on Gt",
      "issue": "conflicting",
      "description": "The main evolution problem, Sec. 3, and the strong formulation in Appendix A.1 prescribe φ=1; the standard-wave weak formulation in Appendix A.1 instead prescribes φv+1=0.",
      "readings": [
        "Impose φ=1 on Gt",
        "Impose φ=0 on Gt"
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "History term in the wave update",
      "issue": "conflicting",
      "description": "Eq. (32), the subsequent weak and matrix forms, and Appendix A.1 use −φv−1. Eq. (34) instead prints −φv, changing the update even when m=k=0.",
      "readings": [
        "Use right-hand side −Sv+2φv−φv−1",
        "Follow Eq. (34) literally and use right-hand side −Sv+φv"
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "Sensitivity normalization Cv",
      "issue": "vague",
      "description": "Eq. (44) places an L²(D)-annotated magnitude inside another domain integral, leaving unclear whether a pointwise magnitude or a global norm is intended. Let a(x) denote the state-equation sensitivity density.",
      "readings": [
        "Cv=(cf V0)^−1 times the integral of |a(x)| over D",
        "Read the inner expression as a global L² norm, giving Cv=cf^−1 sqrt(integral of a(x)² over D)"
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "Initial augmented-Lagrangian multiplier",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Sec. 4.1 gives multiplier updates but does not specify the initial λ.",
      "readings": [
        "λ0=0",
        "λ0 equal to the compliance of the initially filled domain"
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "Augmented-Lagrangian penalty continuation",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Sec. 4.1 says r increases each iteration until rmax, but supplies neither its initial value, growth rule, nor cap.",
      "readings": [
        "In the chosen objective units, r0=1 and rnext=min(1.1r,100)",
        "In the chosen objective units, r0=10 and rnext=min(2r,10000)"
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "Ordering of multiplier, penalty, and level-set updates",
      "issue": "vague",
      "description": "Sec. 3 describes updating λ and φ, while Sec. 4.1 distinguishes λ from its previous value without iteration-indexing the multiplier in f1 or specifying when r increases.",
      "readings": [
        "Evaluate f1 using the incoming multiplier and penalty, then update λ, r, and φ",
        "Update λ first and evaluate f1 using that updated multiplier before advancing φ",
        "Increase r first, update λ with the increased penalty, then evaluate f1 and advance φ"
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "Termination of the Sec. 4.1.1 runs",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Sec. 3 mentions convergence or a predefined iteration limit, but provides no convergence measure, tolerances, observation window, or iteration cap.",
      "readings": [
        "Stop after 1000 iterations",
        "Stop when relative compliance change and positive volume violation are below 10^−3 for 10 iterations, with a 500-iteration cap",
        "Use corresponding tolerances of 10^−5 and a 2000-iteration cap"
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "mesh",
      "entity": "Structured-grid dimensions and spacing",
      "issue": "vague",
      "description": "Sec. 4.1 gives only minimum and maximum element sizes, and Sec. 3 uses adaptive mmg refinement. These do not specify grid counts, a spatial mesh-size distribution, or a unique equivalent fixed structured grid.",
      "readings": [
        "100×100 uniform cells with spacing 0.01 m",
        "200×200 uniform cells with spacing 0.005 m",
        "2000×2000 uniform cells with spacing 0.0005 m"
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "mesh",
      "entity": "Finite-element spaces and integration of projected material",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Sec. 3 introduces generic shape functions but does not identify element families, polynomial degrees, quadrature, or where Θ is evaluated. The stated Sobolev order α=2 does not uniquely specify these choices.",
      "readings": [
        "Bilinear Q1 displacement and level-set fields, 2×2 Gauss integration, Θ evaluated at Gauss points",
        "Quadratic Q2 fields, 3×3 Gauss integration, Θ evaluated at Gauss points",
        "Structured cells split into P1 triangles, with Θ evaluated at triangle centroids"
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    }
  ]
}
